authorization: User approved proceeding with the comparison stage. No material behavior or format interpretation changed.

retention.databases: Exact whole opened PMR/MDB files in RAM, implemented by the earlier Canon2 stage.
retention.mxf: Exact bytes returned to the same MxfReader, with original offsets and physical extent; source details are reconstructed with the same reader from RAM.
retention.unreadPayloads: Existing skipped payload ranges remain ranges; this does not retain all original header bytes or skipped essence.
retention.incompleteSources: Keep the existing obtained graph archive or unfinished graph; native replay requires a complete consistent acquisition.
retention.compression: Native acquired byte images are currently uncompressed.
retention.rows: MediaFile evidence, values, selections and relationships retain their existing representation.
retention.omf: Existing independent OmfReader and graph archive path; native OMF storage is outside this stage.

fixtureManifest.scope: Byte-identical genuine file copies; databases deliberately not copied to exercise existing header fallback. No reader or production scheduler change.
fixtureManifest.wholeFileCopyEquality: Whole-file SHA-256 equality checked at copying; original range equality independently checked in the full engine comparison.

verification.priorHeaderBaseline: Pre-change scan-mode file/evidence, scheduling, issue, callback and state hashes, CSV and source stamps match the current default Canon proof. No pre-change full graph proof is asserted.

nativeDatabaseByteProof.scope: Every opened Canon2 PMR/MDB image directly compared byte-for-byte with its unchanged original file in the full run. Timing trials do not repeat this proof.

nativeMxfByteProof.scope: Every retained Canon2 MXF byte range directly compared with its unchanged original at the same original offset in the full run. Range hashes frame original offsets and lengths. Recording payloads outside those acquired ranges are not read for this proof. Timing trials do not repeat this proof.

performance.definition: Medians use only three scan-mode trials per engine. Negative changePercent means Canon2 uses less time/memory. Current and peak process counters are sampled by the probe before verification/CSV; absent counters are not treated as zero.

header-comparison.method: Eight sequential fresh processes using one Release probe linked to both engines: full Canon then full Canon2; three scan-only pairs ordered Canon/Canon2, Canon2/Canon, Canon/Canon2. Filesystem cache is uncontrolled. No Windows/NEXIS or cold-cache claim follows from a macOS run.

proofScope.full: Complete recursive graphs, alias topology, projections, direct original-reader equality, exact Canon2 native database bytes and original-offset/byte equality for every retained MXF range, plus scan/CSV evidence.
proofScope.scan: Final row/evidence, scheduling, issues, callbacks, completion, CSV and unchanged input stamps. Source graph/projection/original-byte verification is omitted.
proofScope.storage: Representation differences are reported separately. Canon2 requires zero database archives and unfinished graphs. Complete, valid MXF reads retain native acquired ranges; non-complete/invalid MXF reads and legacy media keep graph archives. Acquired bytes include rereads; captured bytes count unique retained positions. No picture/sound payload retention policy is changed.

measurementScope.csv: Existing Canon adapter and MediaCsv with precompute details and clip duration enabled; created after memory sample.
measurementScope.memory: Fresh-process current resident/physical footprint or Windows private bytes and peak resident sampled immediately after scan return, retaining session; before graph restoration, original rereads and adapter rows. Peak includes process setup, preflight discovery and the scan. Unsupported counters are omitted.
measurementScope.scan: Synchronous engine scan including discovery, readers, storage, projection, matching and selection; excludes verification and CSV adapters.
measurementScope.setup: Common preflight discovery enumerates input stamps before timing. Its inventory is released before memoryBefore; stamps and bounded callback sink remain. Filesystem cache is uncontrolled; no cold-cache claim.
measurementScope.verification: Full mode verifies every recursive retained graph and projection plus fresh direct-reader original comparisons for opened sources. One graph at a time. Exact native database bytes and each acquired MXF range compared directly to unchanged source files. MXF range hashes include original offsets and lengths; bytes outside those acquired ranges are not read for this byte proof. The established reader still excludes recognized picture/sound payloads. All property fields, read coverage, observations, selections, stamps, issues, callbacks and alias topology hashed; storage representation excluded from semantic hashes.

buildReceipt.configurationEvidence: Recorded CMake cache settings and probe location; no build flags inferred from filenames.

header-comparison.attribution: No databases are present; this collection isolates the MXF storage change.

limitations: Local macOS arm64 Release measurements; filesystem cache uncontrolled. Three alternating fresh-process scan-mode pairs per collection.
Process memory counters are sampled before source restoration, original-reader/byte verification, CSV creation and GUI row adaptation. They are not a complete GUI application memory measurement.
No 300,000-file Windows/NEXIS completion or memory-fit claim; real-workload qualification remains.
Native source payload totals exclude allocator, container and row-evidence overhead.
The existing reader still expands one source temporarily. This stage changes retained storage, not that temporary decoding cost.
No new read scope, format interpretation, metadata policy, live-engine promotion or retirement of old readers/tests.

documentationExtraction.scope: Preserved measured format/source facts and current-reader results; removed superseded implementation references. This is an extracted receipt, not a new verification or a renamed source-code fingerprint.
